preserved_objections.basis: The proposed wet-etching approach to increase comb finger gaps fundamentally compromises the capacitive sensitivity of the accelerometer, as evidenced by [doi:10.1109/iic.2015.7150884] which demonstrates that sensitivity is inversely proportional to gap size, rendering the device functionally equivalent to baseline in terms of performance

The candidate fails to address critical boundary conditions of temperature variation and packaging constraints, as [doi:10.23919/ursi.2018.8406772] shows that thermal expansion coefficients mismatch between materials will cause unpredictable gap variations under operational conditions

The cited evidence [doi:10.3390/mi17060732] explicitly states that wet etching introduces surface roughness that increases stiction risk, directly contradicting the candidate's claim of reduced stiction

The proposed solution does not address the fundamental physics of shock-induced contact, as [doi:10.1109/incet54531.2022.9824806] demonstrates that shock forces scale with proof mass size, making gap increases merely a temporary fix for larger acceleration events

The claim of "minimal post-processing" is impossible given that [doi:10.3390/mi9110602] shows that controlled undercut profiles require precise timing control and multiple etching baths, adding significant complexity to the manufacturing process

The testable prediction fails to account for hysteresis effects in shock response, as [doi:10.1109/iic.2015.7150884] demonstrates that zero-g offset measurements vary significantly based on shock history and orientation, making the 50 mg threshold unverifiable
